7 PROCUREMENT AND CONTRACT MANAGEMENT

### 7.1. Procurement Assessment

In 2022, the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan has modernized its procurement framework by issuing Regulations No. 8 and 15 that further align with the digitization, sustainability and anti-corruption agendas. The Jordanian e-procurement system (www.joneps.gov.jo) is operational for centralized procurement. Despite presence of several policy papers, guidance documents, and instructions, there is no compiled manual that guides practitioners and economic operators on public procurement. Despite issuance of new standard procurement documents for goods and works in 2024, the public sector still lacks a standard request for proposals for consulting services. There are, however, standard forms of contract for engineering design and supervision services.

Procurement risks relate mainly to vague international publicity requirements, limited use of e-procurement, absence of tangible sustainability practices, limited types of standard procurement documents, absence of strategic procurement planning, absence of SECAP monitoring experiences, challenges associated with grant management, and dilution of responsibilities among multiple procurement committees and project stakeholders. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
